guidelines: Provider facts must be independently revalidated at receipt creation and PR audit; a user-supplied file or creation-time-only check is insufficient.
Recovery authority must remain finite, path-bound, archive-preserving, and unable to authorize merge, release, branch deletion, provider mutation, or threshold weakening.
Keep source runtime, installed template, agent rules, documentation, and generated capability projections aligned.

intent.problem: PR #716 contains a completed immutable #709 archive and all tests pass, yet GitHub template-smoke correctly failed at 85.09% against the 85.10% aggregate coverage floor. The existing post-archive recovery command requires local check-ai-pr to fail, so it cannot open a receipt for this hosted-only failure; manually supplying a receipt or committing tests to the archived PR would bypass governance.
constraints: Bind the existing GitHub failure to exact repository, PR, candidate Head, run/job, provider outcomes, log content, and archive evidence; revalidate those facts in check-ai-pr.
Do not rewrite #709 archive evidence, lower/exclude coverage, hand-write evidence, or make an ad-hoc commit to PR #716.
Do not create a new GitHub Issue; this corrective Work Item remains bound to Issue #709.
Update source and installed template runtime/docs/agent guidance together.
intent.rationale: A provider-revalidated receipt closes the specific lifecycle gap while preserving immutable evidence and a narrow, auditable recovery path. It lets #709 obtain meaningful coverage tests after the corrective implementation is merged, rather than replaying or disguising the failed delivery.
